Washington County at a glance

The southwest corner of Utah belongs to Washington County, which touches Arizona on the south and Nevada on the west. St. George has been the seat since 1856. The county is 2,430 square miles and among the fastest-growing in Utah: 90,354 people in 2000, 138,115 in 2010 and 180,279 in 2020, with a 2025 estimate of 213,670. About 73.0% of households own their home.

Iron County is to the north and Kane County to the east. Utah's lowest elevation, 2,178 feet at Beaver Dam Wash, is in this county. The territorial legislature created Washington County on March 3, 1852, and its boundaries have stood since March 10, 1892.

With 95,342 residents in 2020, St. George is the biggest city outside the Wasatch Front. Santa Clara and Ivins lie west of it, Washington to the east, and Hurricane and La Verkin farther out. Smaller places cluster near Zion and across the north and west. Inside St. George there are more than 20 neighborhoods, including Bloomington, Little Valley, Southgate, Sunbrook, The Ledges, Desert Color and Stone Cliff, so name yours whenever someone is valuing the property. Big irrigated farms in eastern St. George and Washington have given way to housing and commercial lots.

Heat and flood history

Heat comes first on any Washington County inspection list, then water. In St. George the average July afternoon reaches 101.9 degrees, around 60 afternoons a year top 100, and the rain gauge collects only about 8.8 inches. Monsoon storms arrive between early July and mid-September, and a January 2005 flood on the Santa Clara River destroyed 28 homes.

Elevation changes the story. Pine Valley often collects more than 20 inches of precipitation a year. Expect buyers to ask about an aging cooling system and about any lot near a wash or river.

Which county offices handle property tax

Billing and collection belong to the treasurer, while valuation appeals go through the auditor. Both offices are at 111 East Tabernacle Street in St. George, UT 84770.

OfficeHandlesPhone
TreasurerTax notices, payments, delinquent taxes(435) 301-7720
AuditorBoard of Equalization, Tax Commission appeal forms(435) 301-7220
County AdministrationGeneral county contact(435) 301-7000

Every year real property tax comes due on November 30, whether or not a notice reached you. The county mails each owner a notice and sends payment details to the mortgage company, yet checking the notice for mistakes is your job. When neighbors received one and you did not, ask the treasurer for a copy.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Washington County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Partial and late payments

You can send the treasurer a partial payment of $10 or more per parcel whenever you like. The money is applied to interest first, penalty second and tax last. With more than one delinquent year, Utah law makes you pay the newest year first.

Do not count on a payment plan, because the treasurer does not offer them for delinquent taxes. In May the clerk-auditor sells properties that have been delinquent at least five years, announcing the sale in a newspaper roughly four weeks earlier. Tax liens and tax lien certificates cannot be sold under Utah law. Relief programs, among them a circuit breaker program and indigent and hardship abatements, go through the clerk-auditor.

  • Pay the newest year first when several are open.
  • Send at least $10 per parcel if you can only make a partial payment.
  • Call the treasurer before the May sale if a parcel is close to five years behind.

How to appeal your property value

A request for review goes to the Board of Equalization. Utah sets the filing deadline at the later of September 15 or 45 days after the county auditor's notice, and the board then has 60 days from your application to rule.

The application needs your own estimate of fair market value, plus whatever shows that your assessment is out of step with comparable homes. Open the auditor's appeal page when summer starts, because that is where the county posts the close of each year's window. Mid-September is too late to find out you missed it.

Disagree with the board? File Form TC-194 with the county auditor within 30 days of the Notice of Determination, and the auditor forwards it to the Utah State Tax Commission.

Property tax when you sell

Washington County tax is a lien on the parcel, so the bill stays with the house when ownership changes. If the sale closes mid-year, the title company prorates the year's tax, and the settlement statement lists each side's share.

  • Search your parcel in the county's tax notice lookup at outpost.washco.utah.gov.
  • Check whether your lender's escrow account already paid this year.
  • Have the treasurer confirm any back balance before the closing date. Delinquent taxes get paid newest year first.
  • Give the treasurer a new mailing address so notices do not collect at an empty house.

Inherited houses, vacation homes and rentals in St. George and Hurricane make up most of the calls we take. We buy Washington County houses as-is. When back taxes are involved, the balance is paid from proceeds at closing and you see the figure before deciding, so you never bring cash to the table. A cash sale also skips showings and the wait on a buyer's mortgage, and you choose the closing date. Bring the deed, the latest notice and the parcel number to the first conversation.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Washington County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Where to call first

Call the treasurer at (435) 301-7720 about the amount owed, an older delinquent year or a notice that never came. Valuation and Board of Equalization questions go to the auditor at (435) 301-7220, and anything else can start at County Administration, (435) 301-7000. All three offices are at 111 East Tabernacle Street in St. George.

Because the board must rule within 60 days of an application, and a Tax Commission appeal must be filed within 30 days of the Notice of Determination, a seller with a sale pending should not leave a value dispute for the last minute. If a closing is near, ask the treasurer for the tax figure and hand it to the title company so the settlement statement matches.

Not sure where your Washington County house stands? It costs nothing to ask. Send us the parcel number and the most recent notice, and tell us whether the house is occupied, vacant, inherited or rented. We will look at the balance, tell you what an as-is purchase would involve, and leave the decision with you.

Frequently asked questions

When are Washington County, Utah property taxes due?

Real property tax is due November 30 every year, even if you did not receive a notice. The treasurer accepts partial payments of $10 or more per parcel at any time. The office is at 111 East Tabernacle Street in St. George.

How do I appeal my Washington County property value?

File an application with the county Board of Equalization by the later of September 15 or 45 days after the auditor gives notice. Include your own value estimate and comparable evidence. The auditor's office at (435) 301-7220 can confirm the current year's window.

What if I disagree with the Board of Equalization decision?

Appeal to the Utah State Tax Commission with Form TC-194, filed with the county auditor within 30 days after the Notice of Determination.

Does Washington County sell tax liens?

No. Utah law does not allow tax liens or lien certificates to be sold. Instead, the clerk-auditor holds a sale each May for properties delinquent at least five years.

Who pays the property tax when a Washington County house sells?

The title company prorates the tax at closing, and your settlement statement shows the split. We buy houses as-is in Washington County and can work with whatever tax balance is owed.

Selling in Salt Lake County? Get a Cash Offer

Last updated November 14, 2026.

Selling in Salt Lake County?

Salt Lake County at a glance

No Utah county has more people. Salt Lake City is the seat, and the 2025 estimate of 1,220,916 follows a 2020 count of 1,185,238. Whether your house is in Sandy, Murray, Herriman, Holladay, Millcreek, Midvale, Taylorsville, Riverton, Bluffdale, South Salt Lake or one of the larger cities such as West Valley City, West Jordan, South Jordan, Draper and Cottonwood Heights, or out in Magna, Kearns or Copperton, one county tax system bills it. Every date and office below applies.

Earthquake questions come up in this valley because the Wasatch Fault follows the mountain front. Past foundation repair, chimney work or a seismic retrofit deserves a folder of receipts you can hand to the buyer.

Which county office does what

Valuation starts with the Assessor, who appraises as of January 1 and completes the roll by May 22. About July 22 the Auditor mails each owner a Notice of Valuation and Tax Change. After that, three offices matter.

  • Treasurer sends bills, collects payments and administers relief. Visit 2001 S State St, Suite N1-200, call 385-468-8300 or write treasurer@saltlakecounty.gov. Weekday hours are 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. For relief questions, press option 2 on the same number.
  • Recorder files deeds and other documents, in Suite N1-600 of the same building at 2001 S State St. Phone 385-468-8145.
  • Board of Equalization decides value disputes. It sits at 2002 S State St, #N3-300, with mail going to PO Box 144575.

Due dates and penalties

Pay by November 30 and there is no penalty. A weekend or holiday pushes that to the following business day. By law, bills go in the mail no later than November 1.

  • January 1: appraisal and ownership are fixed for the year.
  • Around July 22: owners receive valuation notices.
  • August 1: appeals open at the Board of Equalization.
  • September 15: appeals close, unless 45 days after your notice falls later.
  • December 1: anything unpaid is delinquent.
  • January 31: the penalty rises when a balance remains.

The first penalty, charged December 1, is 2.5% or $10 per parcel, whichever is more. Clear the full balance by January 31 and it falls to 1% or $10, again the larger. Wait longer and it goes back to 2.5% with interest running from January 1. A December or January closing means asking escrow whether the bill is settled.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Salt Lake County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

How the residential exemption works when a house sells

Utah knocks 45% off the taxable value of a primary home, leaving 55% of market value to tax. To count, the house must be someone's main residence for 183 consecutive days or more in the calendar year, whether the owner or a full-time tenant lives there. Each household gets one.

A new owner does not inherit the break. The buyer files a new declaration, using Form TC-473A starting January 1, 2027, by September 15 with the Board of Equalization. Without it the house may be taxed on 100% of market value that year. Mention it to your buyer when the contract is signed.

How to appeal your valuation

Disputes about value go to the county Board of Equalization, with September 15 as the yearly cutoff. Walk-in filings must arrive by 5:00 p.m. that day. Mail needs that day's postmark. Online submissions can be completed until 11:59 p.m.

  • Send the signed application and every exhibit to propertytaxappeals@saltlakecounty.gov, or mail the packet to 2002 S State St #N3-300.
  • Good exhibits: three or more recent comparable sales, a professional appraisal, proof of mistakes in county records, or your own purchase papers.
  • Bought within the window from July 1 of last year to June 30 of this year? Your closing statement is often the best proof.

Independent hearing officers review what you submit and recommend an outcome. The Board then raises, lowers or leaves the value alone. Keep paying on schedule while you wait, since refunds follow only a final ruling. If you disagree with the Board, the State Tax Commission accepts an appeal within 30 days.

Tax relief programs

Six Treasurer programs help owners who meet age, income or status tests. Forms open on January 1 and are due by September 1.

Treasurer relief programs and who qualifies
ProgramWho qualifies
Circuit BreakerAge 67 or older, or a surviving spouse, with household income up to $44,221
Indigent ReliefAge 65 or older or receiving disability benefits, with income and assets below $44,221
Senior DeferralHomeowners age 75 or older meeting income and asset rules
Disabled Veteran ReliefOwners with a service-related disability, or out-of-state active duty members
Blind ReliefLegally blind owners and certain survivors
Hardship ReliefExtreme hardship, subject to income and asset limits

Any deferral or relief claim on a house you are selling alters the payoff, so phone the Treasurer well before closing.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Salt Lake County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

What happens when tax goes unpaid?

Ignore tax long enough and the county sells the property. Redemption ends March 15 in the fifth year after delinquency, and the Auditor then holds the final sale on the fourth Thursday of May. You may still pay right up until that sale.

A newspaper carries the notice for four weeks, and copies are mailed to owners and other interested parties. Facing this, request an exact payoff from the Treasurer. Closing a sale before redemption expires lets escrow settle the balance from your proceeds, often the tidiest way out.

Recording a deed in Salt Lake County

Each recording costs a flat $40, and the paper must follow formatting and notary rules. Go to Suite N1-600 at 2001 South State Street on a weekday between 8:00 a.m. and 5:00 p.m.

  • Black print on one side of white 8.5 by 11 inch paper.
  • Leave a 2.5 by 4.5 inch blank box at the top right of page one.
  • Include the parcel serial number, the legal description and where the grantee lives.
  • Sign in ink, with a notary acknowledgment and a stamp that can be read.

A standard closing leaves all this to the title company. A deed signed elsewhere, like one passed between relatives, must meet the same rules.

Selling with a tax bill pending

Until paid, property tax sits as a lien on the house, and the title company checks its status before closing. Pull together the newest notice, proof of payment and any relief or deferral papers. Remind the buyer to file the new declaration by September 15 if your home had the exemption. Selling for cash removes the lender, not the tax search, so tidy payment records help the closing move faster.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Frequently asked questions

When are Salt Lake County property taxes due?

Pay by November 30 to avoid a penalty. If that day is a weekend or holiday, the next business day counts. Tax unpaid on December 1 is delinquent.

What is the deadline to appeal a Salt Lake County value?

September 15, or 45 days after your valuation notice is mailed when that comes later. File with the Board of Equalization.

Does the Utah residential exemption transfer to the buyer?

No. A buyer has to submit a new declaration, and a late or absent one can put the house at 100% of market value for the year.

How much does it cost to record a deed in Salt Lake County?

Recording costs $40 flat, plus $2 for each legal description beyond 10. Copies of a recorded document are $2 a page.

Can I get property tax relief as a senior?

Possibly. Circuit Breaker relief covers ages 67 and up with income up to $44,221, and Senior Deferral covers owners 75 and older. Call 385-468-8300, option 2, to check eligibility.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

Selling in Tooele County?
We buy Tooele County houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.

Tooele County at a glance

Northwestern Utah holds Tooele County, just west of Salt Lake County. It spans 7,286 square miles, making it the state's second biggest and among its driest. The population lives mostly in a band along the eastern edge, between the Oquirrh and Stansbury ranges, while the western half is open desert with Interstate 80 running through it.

The headcount was 40,735 in 2000, 58,218 in 2010 and 72,698 in 2020. More and more residents drive into the Salt Lake Valley for work. Two homes with the same Tooele County mailing address can be worlds apart, say a lot in town and acreage at the desert's edge, and the assessor values each on its own.

Towns and areas in the county

Tooele is the seat and the biggest city, with Grantsville next. Erda, Lake Point, Stockton, Rush Valley, Wendover and Ibapah are smaller.

  • Tooele had 35,742 residents in 2020. It climbs the western slope of the Oquirrhs at about 4,915 feet and is roughly 40 minutes from Salt Lake City.
  • Grantsville had 12,617 residents in 2020 and sits near 4,265 feet. State Route 138 carries traffic to Interstate 80 and east toward Stansbury Park.
  • Stansbury Park grew from 5,145 people in 2010 to 9,851 in 2020. It is unincorporated, so the county supplies most services, and it lies about six miles north of Tooele on State Route 36.
  • Wendover had 1,115 residents in 2020 and shares a border with West Wendover, Nevada.

Stansbury Park started in 1970 as a planned community built around a golf course and a man-made lake. The Stansbury Park Improvement District supplies water and sewer, and the Stansbury Park Community Association gives preliminary sign-off to housing and remodeling plans. Owners there should expect buyers to ask about association rules at the start.

Weather and your house

Hot dry summers meet cold, snowy winters, and roofs, heating systems and paint take the beating. January normals reach a high of 38.7 degrees and July normals 91.4. A typical year brings about 18.44 inches of precipitation and 75.3 inches of snow. The record high stands at 106 degrees and the record low at minus 16. Wendover gets only about 4.58 inches of precipitation a year.

Inspectors tend to start with the roof, the furnace and the water heater, and then move on to settling and the grading around the foundation. Homes that sit empty through several winters show more damage. If you sell as-is, you do not pay for those repairs.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Tooele County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Property tax calendar

Value is set as of January 1 each year. The county mails valuation notices in July or August, and payment is penalty-free through November 30.

DateStep in the tax year
January 1Value is fixed as of this day
May 22Assessor finishes the roll and hands values to the Auditor
May or JuneCounty tax sale of parcels five or more years behind
July or AugustValuation notices go in the mail
August or SeptemberAppeals to the Board of Equalization, within 45 days of the notice
By November 1Tax notices arrive
November 30Final day to pay with no penalty
December 1Anything unpaid is delinquent

Check the county's assessor dates page for the posted schedule. For questions, call the Treasurer's office, 47 S. Main Street in Tooele, at (435) 843-3190 on weekdays between 8:00 am and 5:00 pm.

Appealing your valuation

Your window to file with the county Board of Equalization is 45 days from when your Notice of Property Valuation was mailed, or September 15. Your appeal must include at least one of these:

  • Comparable sales of similar homes that closed before January 1 at prices below your assessed value.
  • A closing statement for a purchase before January 1, plus a bank-required appraisal if it was a short sale, bank-owned sale or foreclosure.
  • An appraisal whose effective date falls within the year.
  • A written description of a factual error in the record, such as the wrong square footage or a carport recorded as a garage.

Complaining about the size of the bill will not win an appeal. Rates are set by the cities, school districts and other districts after public budget hearings. When the board rules against you, send a written appeal to the State Tax Commission through the county auditor within 30 days of that decision. In its appeals publication, the Commission estimates a typical homeowner saves $4 to $8 in tax per $1,000 of value removed.

The residential exemption and a sale

A primary home that qualifies is taxed on 55 percent of its market value. That break does not pass to the next owner on its own. It applies to up to one acre per residential unit, depends on primary residence use, and allows part-year use if it totals at least 183 consecutive days. A household gets one exemption.

After a sale the buyer must apply using Form TC-473A, sent to assessorsurvey@tooeleco.gov. When the form is not returned in 30 days, the county mails a notice and gives 30 more days. After that the exemption is dropped. From January 1, 2027, any change in ownership interest, deeds and trust transfers included, requires a fresh form under 2026 SB 238, and applications are due to the Board of Equalization by September 15. Without the exemption the property is taxed at 100 percent of market value, a point heirs and landlords selling a Tooele County rental should know before listing.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Tooele County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Selling with taxes owed

A balance unpaid on December 1 is delinquent, with penalties and interest piling on, and a parcel more than five years behind can be sold at the tax sale. In the 2022 cycle, 1,946 delinquency notices went out and nearly $5.5 million remained unpaid on December 31. The penalty started at the greater of 1 percent or $10 and rose to the greater of 2.5 percent or $10 after January 31, with 10 percent interest on the December 1 balance. Call the Treasurer for what applies this year, since penalty and interest rules can change.

The Auditor advertises the tax sale weekly for four weeks, and owners may redeem before it happens. If you are behind and want out, call us before the delinquency list comes out. We get the payoff from the Treasurer and build the closing around it. The balance is paid from your proceeds at the closing table, and you see the number in writing first.

Have the latest tax notice, the July valuation notice and the deed ready when you call. Heirs and landlords should add any exemption paperwork.

Frequently asked questions

When are Tooele County property taxes due?

Real property tax for the current year is penalty-free through November 30. On December 1 unpaid tax is delinquent. The county sends notices before November 1.

What is the deadline to appeal a Tooele County property valuation?

Whichever is later: September 15, or 45 days from the mailing date of the valuation notice. Send the Board of Equalization your evidence, such as comparable sales, an appraisal, a closing statement or proof of a factual error.

Do I lose the 45 percent residential exemption when I sell?

As the seller you lose it at the sale, and the buyer must file a new application. If none is approved, the full market value can be taxed.

Where is the Tooele County Treasurer?

47 S. Main Street, Tooele, UT 84074. Call (435) 843-3190 between 8:00 am and 5:00 pm, Monday through Friday.

Can you buy a Tooele County house with back taxes owed?

Yes. We obtain a current balance from the Treasurer and handle it through closing. Houses anywhere in the county qualify, from Tooele and Grantsville to Stansbury Park.

Selling in Wasatch County?

Wasatch County at a glance

Heber Valley, a basin ringed by mountains on the Wasatch Back, is the heart of Wasatch County in north central Utah. Heber City serves as seat and biggest city. Midway is here too, along with a piece of Park City. Neighbors are Salt Lake, Summit, Duchesne and Utah counties, and over half the land lies above 7,500 feet.

The population was 8,523 in 1980, 34,788 in 2020 and about 38,514 in the 2025 estimate, and the 2020 count was 47.8% above the 2010 count. About 76.3% of households own their home. Heber City, 43 miles southeast of Salt Lake City at 5,601 feet, had 16,856 residents in 2020, and about 27% of them commute to Park City or Salt Lake City. Midway had 6,003 residents. Some Midway subdivisions require a share of Swiss-style features on new houses, so ask about design rules if you inherit or list a home there.

Winters and your house

Long, snowy winters mean buyers look first at the roof, the furnace and exposed pipes. Heber City gets about 75 inches of snow a year over roughly 29 snowy days, with January and December the heaviest months at 21.5 and 17.8 inches. The average January high is 36.5 degrees and the average January low is 12.5, the record low is minus 38, and the average July high is near 89.5.

Snow is not a flaw. Still, an inspector can easily spot postponed roof, gutter or heating work on an older Heber Valley house. If the house needs that work and you would rather not pay for it first, an as-is cash purchase is a common answer.

Who runs property tax in Wasatch County

Three offices split the work. The assessor sets values, the clerk/auditor calculates rates and handles value appeals, and the treasurer collects payment. The county council doubles as the Board of Equalization that rules on those appeals.

Utah taxes property at 100% of fair market value as of January 1. If you occupy the home for 183 or more consecutive days in the year, a 45% primary residence exemption applies. Farmland that qualifies can be valued by what it produces, with greenbelt applications due May 1. Before a taxing entity can raise the revenue it collects, it has to hold a public hearing, and individual rates shift when county-wide values shift. The county's property tax system page explains the system in full.

Property tax calendar

Valuation happens January 1 and the cycle ends with tax hearings in December.

DateEvent

Read the July valuation notice closely each year, since it is your first look at the new value. If the number looks wrong, the appeal window runs from August 1 to September 15, so do not let the notice sit in a pile of mail. A seller who appeals before listing may also give buyers a lower, better supported tax figure.

Paying, and what late costs

Mail a payment postmarked on or before November 30 and there is no penalty. The treasurer accepts online payment through Instant Payments but no credit cards.

  • A payment received between December 1 and January 31 draws a 1% penalty.
  • A payment postmarked after January 31 draws a 2.5% penalty plus interest back to January 1.
  • Make checks out to Wasatch County Treasurer, mail them to 25 N. Main, Heber City, UT 84032, and write the parcel number on the check.

Walk-in hours are 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. on weekdays, and the main line is (435) 657-3218. Ask your mortgage company whether it pays the tax for you. People often lose track of that after a refinance or a sale of the loan.

An updated list of multiyear delinquent accounts goes up on the county site every week. Interest accrues all the time, so a payoff figure changes daily. For the exact number, call (435) 657-3217.

How to appeal your valuation

Get your appeal to the clerk/auditor by 5 p.m. on September 15. You can file online or at 25 North Main Street in Heber City. The state rule is the later of September 15 or 45 days after notice from the county, and the county board then has 60 days to decide.

Attach proof. The county denies any application that lacks evidence of your own value estimate. Parcels can be combined in one appeal when the owner is the same and they lie in the same general area, though every parcel needs its own supporting evidence. You can reach the clerk/auditor at (435) 657-3190.

When the board's decision goes against you, the Utah State Tax Commission hears a further appeal. File Form TC-194 with the county auditor within 30 days of the county's decision. The governing statute is Utah Code 59-2-1004.

Taxes when you sell a Wasatch County house

Request the payoff from the treasurer before you sign anything, and compare it with the closing statement. The weekly delinquent listing is the fastest way to see whether your parcel is on it.

  • Pull your latest tax notice and the July valuation notice.
  • Ask the mortgage servicer if an escrow account already covered this year.
  • Call (435) 657-3217 on the day you plan to close and get the current payoff.
  • For an empty house or seasonal home, update the mailing address so notices find you.

Back taxes, deferred repairs or the cost of carrying a second home are common reasons people want out. We buy houses in Wasatch County as-is and can work around all of them. Frequently asked questions

How much is Wasatch County property tax due and when?

The due date is November 30, and anything postmarked by then is penalty-free. Tax notices are mailed on October 30. The amount depends on your assessed value and the combined rate of every taxing entity that covers your address.

Does Wasatch County give a break for a primary residence?

Yes. Utah applies a 45% exemption to a home you occupy for 183 or more consecutive days in a year. Send residential exemption forms to the Assessor's Office before June.

When is the deadline to appeal my Wasatch County property value?

The county board accepts appeals from August 1 through September 15 at 5 p.m. Evidence of your own value estimate has to arrive with the form. File online or at the clerk/auditor's office at 25 North Main Street in Heber City.

Can I pay Wasatch County property tax by credit card?

No. You can pay online through Instant Payments, mail a check to 25 N. Main, Heber City, or visit the office on a weekday between 8:00 a.m. and 5:00 p.m.

Can I sell a Wasatch County house if the taxes are unpaid?

In most cases, yes. Get the payoff amount from the treasurer at (435) 657-3217, and pay it from the proceeds at closing. We buy houses in Wasatch County as-is, so a tax balance does not stop us from making an offer.
